title.en: An execution log records steps and verification, never people

goal.en: Run part of a shakshuka with a person doing one step, then read the log: each step says who verified it, the human intervention is counted in minutes, consent is none by default and time precision is a day.

note.en: Start a shakshuka run with a person present.
The arm cuts; the run waits for a person to heat the pan.
The person heats the pan and confirms.
The heating step completes; the run waits for the next human step.

Four steps ran: three verified by the vision sensor, one by the person. The human intervention appears as a kind and minutes, consent.dataset is none, privacy.personalData is none, timePrecision is day.

outcome.en: You know what a log holds and what it leaves out, which is what makes a research dataset of logs possible with consent. Next: scenario 003 shows the household side of the same principle.
